key_insight: Real patient-chatbot interactions are much more diverse than idealized simulations, and that diversity can materially change triage outcomes in health AI.
engineering_relevance: Health chatbot evaluation and deployment should model patient communication style, emotion, and strategy—not just clinical symptoms—to avoid brittle performance and inequitable care.
method: Analyzed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations to characterize communication diversity.
Built a patient simulator that separates clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style.
Tested four LLMs across five patient personae in 1,164 clinician-graded urgency-assessment cases.
evidence_signal: In a Turing-inspired realism test with 15 human graders, simulated conversations were nearly indistinguishable from real ones, with graders scoring only 55% accuracy.
watch_item: Simulated or benchmarked patients that are too cooperative or articulate may overestimate chatbot performance and miss real-world disparities in urgent care triage.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
